title: From RL to IRL — Gaurav Mishra, Amazon AGI Lab
talk_summary: A researcher from Amazon AGI Lab describes what breaks when RL-trained computer-use agents hit real environments: partial observability, irreversibility, non-determinism, ephemeral credentials, ambiguous success, and adversarial content. Their fix is to model real-world messiness into training and to add harness-level guardrails (checkpointing, risk classifiers, execution monitors, audit logs, human handoff) that thin out as the model improves.

takeaways.technique: Recovery as a native agent action, not a reset
takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of resetting state on infra errors, they pass the error to the model and expect it to recover using native actions like refresh, backtrack, wait, abandon, or escalate.
takeaways.evidence_quote: whenever we have an infra error, we pass it to the model and we expect the model to recover from it using native tool use

takeaways.technique: Execution monitor for loops and unproductive behavior
takeaways.what_they_do: The harness watches for bad patterns like model loops, repeated clicks, or unproductive behavior and nudges the model in the right direction.
takeaways.evidence_quote: execution monitor, looking out for any bad patterns from the model loops or repeated clicks or unproductive behavior, and then nudging it

takeaways.what_they_do: A harness layer classifies proposed actions by authorization, irreversibility, and visibility, and forces human handoff when the model's confidence is miscalibrated.
takeaways.evidence_quote: based on if the action is authorized, if it is irreversible, is it visible to the user, what impact it has, we need to teach the model to know when to go for it

takeaways.technique: Process reward, not just outcome reward
takeaways.what_they_do: They penalize dangerous actions anywhere along the trajectory, not only judging the final outcome, because the path and its impact matter.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we focus really hard on making sure we catch all of these dangerous actions throughout the process, not just the outcome, and penalize that accordingly

takeaways.technique: Checkpoint and rollback in the harness
takeaways.what_they_do: Before risky actions the harness checkpoints state so it can roll back to a known-good point if the action goes bad.

takeaways.technique: Adversarial tasks baked into the loop
takeaways.what_they_do: They deliberately test the model with adversarial traps during training so it learns to avoid them, treating this as mainstream rather than a byproduct.
takeaways.evidence_quote: You have to actually test the model during training to make mistakes and then learn learn from them so that it does well in production.
